implementationPlan.description: TDD RED: create the two strict aggregate TypeScript projects and the non-authority security lane smoke before either Vitest config or root script exists. Both tsconfigs extend ../../tsconfig.base.json, disable composite/declaration outputs, retain strict/noEmit behavior and Node types, and include every lane .ts file so helpers/configs cannot escape typechecking. In lane-smoke.security.ts import the actual root/fault/security config objects (never a test-side reimplementation), read the real package.json, and assert exact lane roots, includes/excludes, passWithNoTests:false, stable serial settings, typecheck-before-Vitest script strings, and the root config's existing *.test.ts-only discovery. Assert the smoke's own normalized path/suffix and import no packages/** product surface or authority. Run a focused compile and capture the expected missing-config RED; a syntax error or unrelated failure is not the TDD signal.

Implement tests/fault/vitest.config.ts. Derive a lane-local root from import.meta.url with node:url/path APIs; include foundation/**/*.test.ts and **/*.fault.ts only; spread configDefaults.exclude and explicitly exclude hostile suffixes from the other lane. Pin node environment, forks, isolate:true, passWithNoTests:false, allowOnly:false, retry:0, dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors:false, fileParallelism:false, maxConcurrency:1, and sequence concurrent:false/shuffle:false. Define a small BaseSequencer subclass that sorts a copied TestSpecification array by lane-relative slash-normalized moduleId using a locale-independent code-unit comparator, so cached timings and host locale cannot reorder files. Do not edit tests/fault/foundation/**.
implementationPlan.note:
tests/fault/vitest.config.ts landed, 66 lines, well inside the 250-line target.

SHAPE: root derived lane-locally via dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) — no cwd dependency, no hardcoded separator, portable to macOS/Linux. include ["foundation/**/*.test.ts","**/*.fault.ts"] only. exclude [...configDefaults.exclude, "**/*.security.ts"] — the spread matters because supplying `exclude` REPLACES Vitest's defaults, so dropping it would sweep node_modules. Pinned: environment node, pool forks, isolate true, passWithNoTests false, allowOnly false, retry 0, dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors false, fileParallelism false, maxConcurrency 1, sequence.concurrent false, sequence.shuffle false.

SEQUENCER: FaultLaneSequencer extends BaseSequencer from vitest/node and overrides sort() to return [...files].sort(byModuleId), where byModuleId compares UTF-16 code units of the backslash-normalized moduleId. localeCompare is deliberately not used — its order is host-locale dependent. BaseSequencer's own sort() reads this.ctx.cache and orders by previous-run durations, which is exactly the cached-timing drift the plan wanted removed; the override never calls super.sort. shard() is inherited unchanged.

DEVIATION, order-equivalent and deliberate: the plan said "lane-relative" normalized moduleId; I compare the normalized ABSOLUTE id. Every id in a lane shares the lane-root prefix, and lexicographic comparison of strings with a common prefix is identical after stripping it — so the executed order is provably the same, with one less path computation and no failure mode when an id sits outside the lane root. Nothing else in the step changed.

QA FULL VERIFICATION RECORD.

GATE RE-RUN BY ME: `pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security` -> FINAL=0. Fault 3 files / 43 tests; security 1 file / 17 tests. Matches the recorded evidence exactly.

DoD 3's "A ZERO-CASE LANE EXITS NON-ZERO" — MEASURED, AND I GOT IT WRONG TWICE FIRST. Recording the false starts because either one, reported alone, would have justified a wrong rejection:
1. `--testNamePattern` with no match -> `17 skipped`, exit 0. That is **skipping, not zero-collection**; `passWithNoTests` governs collection. Wrong property.
2. `--dir ./nonexistent-dir` piped to `tail` -> I read `$?` as 0, but that was **tail's** exit, not vitest's. My pipeline swallowed the real code.

Measured correctly, with no pipeline: point the security lane at an empty directory and vitest returns **`REAL_VITEST_EXIT=1`**. `passWithNoTests: false` is load-bearing. The type-error half is satisfied by construction: both scripts are `tsc -p <lane tsconfig> && vitest ...`, so a type error fails before vitest runs, and `tests/security/tsconfig.json` includes `./**/*.ts`.

DoD 1 — MET. `test:fault` and `test:security` each run their own `tsc -p` before their own vitest config. Shell-neutral: `&&` and two binaries, no Unix-only commands. Script preservation verified two ways — the base-ref package.json diff shows only ADDITIONS across the range (test:e2e, test:e2e:browser, test:integration, typecheck:packaging, @playwright/test) with no deletions, and the smoke lane asserts it directly: "preserves every script added by predecessor tasks". Turning DoD 1's preservation clause into an executing assertion rather than a promise is the right move on a shared package.json that three tasks touched today.

DoD 2 — MET, exactly as written. Fault: `include: ["foundation/**/*.test.ts", "**/*.fault.ts"]`, `exclude: [...configDefaults.exclude, "**/*.security.ts"]`. Security: `include: ["**/*.security.ts"]`, `exclude: [...configDefaults.exclude, "**/*.fault.ts", "**/*.test.ts", "**/*.spec.ts"]`. Both lanes exclude the other, both keep vitest's own default excludes rather than replacing them, and both set `passWithNoTests: false`. Determinism is not one setting but six: `fileParallelism: false`, `maxConcurrency: 1`, `sequence.concurrent: false`, `shuffle: false`, `retry: 0`, plus a custom sequencer.

THE SEQUENCER IS THE DETAIL WORTH NAMING. It sorts by UTF-16 code unit on a separator-normalized module id and the comment says why `localeCompare` was rejected: its ordering is host-locale dependent, so it would make the executed order differ between machines. That is DoD 5's portability clause answered in the one place it would actually have bitten — a lane that runs in a different order on a Linux CI box than on this Windows host is not the deterministic lane the DoD asked for. `replaceAll("\\", "/")` handles the separator half.

DoD 3's SMOKE SCOPE — MET. Its cases are runner/config facts only: file identity, the two root scripts, typecheck-ordering, script preservation, both configs' roots/includes/excludes, and fail-empty plus serial ordering. No product behaviour, no security claim. The header states it outright: collecting this lane confers NO security PASS of any kind. That matters for rail 2 — an infrastructure task certifying only lane discovery must not leave an artifact a later reader mistakes for a security gate.

DoD 4 — MET, and verified from the root config rather than assumed. Root `include: ["packages/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.ts"]`. `lane-smoke.security.ts` is the only hostile-suffix file on disk and root structurally cannot match it, so `.security.ts`/`.fault.ts` never become ordinary regression evidence. Meanwhile `tests/fault/foundation/*.test.ts` (j1-linear, j3-crash, j4-replan-stale) still ARE matched by root, so existing Foundation behaviour is preserved — which is the second half of DoD 4 and the half that a stricter root exclude would have broken.

RAIL 3 — no edit to `tests/fault/foundation/**` or the other protected fault trees; the commit's fault-side content is the tsconfig and vitest config only.
